coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 12
record.summary: Planned commercial block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (the design guidelines permit office and laboratory/life-science uses), paired with Block 11 in the project engineer's description of about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking; design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report, with no construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232023, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 12 is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 2,940 m2 against the lot's 2,645 m2; 77% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 85% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 12 is not yet built, which is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says vertical applications are under review for Blocks 11 and 12.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232023 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 12. Lot 4232023 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4232023; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 100 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. Paired with Block 11 on the project's MEP engineer's page (Meyers+), which describes the two blocks together as about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (see that entry for the combined GSF estimate); the final D4D's Table 3.1.1 permits laboratory and life-science uses on Block 12, but no cited source calls the pair a life-science campus. No construction-start source found; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) says vertical applications for Blocks 11 and 12 were under review.

facts.value: Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses permitted; Residential Not Permitted under the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1. The Sept 28, 2026 committee version of the amendment package (passed on first reading Sept 29, 2026; not shown as enacted) would permit residential use on Block 12: the revised legislative digest says 'the ordinance would allow residential uses on Block 12'
flat 100 ft max per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3

The Sept 28, 2026 draft Design for Development attached to the Amended and Restated Development Agreement labels Block 12 '123' Residential Maximum Building Height' and '115' Commercial Maximum Building Height' (Appendix A.11), where the adopted D4D's Appendix A.11 labels it '100' Maximum'. Not shown as enacted as of Oct 12, 2026, so the 100 ft above still governs until then
Blocks 11 and 12 combined: approximately 430,000 sq ft of office, with below-grade parking, per the project's MEP engineer
Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson (Blocks 11, 12 and 15 together)
Seeking LEED Gold certification; designed as an all-electric building

Bus shelter and transit operator restroom delivered with Block 12, per the Phasing Table; a 100% Schematic Design plan set incorporating SFMTA/Public Works feedback was sent to those agencies January 7, 2022
Listed as part of Phase 1 in the 2024 annual compliance report ('Phase 1 includes Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, and 15...')

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 12 (the Planning Commission had voted 5-0 on January 30, 2020 to recommend approval of the project); the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 12 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer, not a Planning Department document; no Planning Commission or Planning Director approval memo for Block 12 was found to confirm or break out this figure.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026; Legistar lists 'Final action: 10/6/2026' and status 'Mayors Office' with the enactment date and number blank (page read Oct 12, 2026), so it is not confirmed as enacted and this record's height and use facts still show the adopted limits.

Whether Blocks 11 and 12 are described as a life-science campus anywhere: the only source that pairs them (Meyers+) describes about 430,000 sq ft of office; the D4D permits laboratory/life-science use on Block 12 but no cited source says that is the plan.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones); enactment is not confirmed.
